long_biography.plain_text:
In 1965, four siblings — Luciano, Giuliana, Carlo and Gilberto — formalised a knitwear venture near Treviso as Benetton Group. Its garment-dyeing model supported rapid international expansion, while provocative campaigns gave the retailer a visual identity recognised far beyond Italy. Gilberto kept a lower public profile than Luciano and concentrated on the financial architecture behind the company.

The stock-market listing released capital for a new phase. Gilberto steered the family holding into motorway concessions, airport services and roadside restaurants, eventually serving as vice-chair of Edizione and chair of Autogrill while sitting on Atlantia's board. Those roles made him the key organiser of an empire no longer dependent on sweaters alone. He remained engaged in its governance until dying at his Treviso home in 2018, aged 77.
